why: fileValues' kv regex splits `https://user:pw@host` at the scheme colon, so the URL password in ~/.git-credentials is never extracted and leaks via `git credential fill`
isSecretValue rejects values starting with `/` as paths even under a secret name, and a base64-alphabet AWS secret key can start with `/`
both fileValues' password regex and URL_PASSWORD require a non-empty username, so the standard `redis://:password@host` form leaks
URL_PASSWORD stops the password at the first `@`, but URL parsers split at the last one, so most of an unencoded `@` password stays visible
values under 12 chars get no base64 variants and redactEncoded needs 16+ (line) or 24+ chars, so a 10-char password's base64 in a k8s Secret passes

why: `.secrets` (nektos/act's default secret file) matches no SECRET_NAMES pattern, so it is read unmasked and its values are never registered
fileValues skips `- item` lines and the token sweep drops 64-hex strings, so a list entry and a hex signing secret in secrets.yaml leak via cat
a one-line JSON object is not a kv line and the token sweep needs 20+ alnum chars, so a password with symbols in minified credentials.json is never registered
projectSecretFiles stops descending at depth 6, so a secrets.yaml seven directories deep in a monorepo is never registered and leaks via cat
a .env value inside docker inspect's JSON Env array is replaced, neighbouring settings survive
`base64 .env` output (76-col wrapped) is decoded and replaced even though the password is short
commit SHAs and lockfile integrity hashes survive while a .env with secrets exists
